title: Majority Element
summary: You get a list of integers `nums`. One value fills more than half of the list: it appears more than len(nums) / 2 times. Return that value. The input always contains such a value, so there is no missing case to handle.

examples.explanation: 5 appears 3 times out of 5, which is more than half.
7 appears 4 times out of 7, while -4 appears only 3 times.

approaches.twist: Count each value in one pass, and return the value whose count is more than half the length of the list.
Keep a candidate and a count that goes up on a match and down otherwise, switching candidates when the count hits zero.
Sort the list and return the value at the middle index, which the answer always covers.
approaches.note: Works, because a value that fills more than half the list must cover the middle, but sorting takes O(n log n) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: Only how often each value appears matters here, not where it sits: tally every value in one pass with a dict or a Counter.
The test is a count against a threshold: Counter(nums) gives each value's count to compare with len(nums) / 2.
The value is guaranteed to exist, and a value that fills more than half the list is also the one that appears most often, so Counter(nums).most_common(1) finds it.

constraintReading: len(nums) can reach 5·10⁴, so counting each value by rescanning the list is O(n²), about 2.5·10⁹ steps: too slow. Sorting to find the middle is O(n log n). One pass with a Counter is O(n) time for O(n) space, and values up to 10⁹ in size rule out an array indexed by value.

related.relation: Counts values with a Counter the same way, then compares two strings' counts instead of checking one count against half the length.
